title.en: Symmetric and public-key cryptography, digital signatures and authentication
title.zh: 对称与公钥密码、数字签名和认证

description.en: Learn how two people who have never met can agree on a key, confirm who the other is, and prove who a message came from: from block cipher modes, RSA and Diffie-Hellman to signatures, certificates and authentication protocols.
description.zh: 懂得两个没见过面的人怎样约定密钥、确认对方、证明消息出自谁：从分组密码的工作模式、RSA 和 Diffie-Hellman，到签名、证书和认证协议。

name.zh: 对称密钥算法：DES 与 AES (symmetric-key algorithms, DES, AES)

name.en: Block cipher modes: ECB, CBC, CFB, stream ciphers and counter mode
name.zh: 分组密码的工作模式：ECB、CBC、CFB、流密码与计数器 (cipher modes)
密钥流重用攻击 (keystream reuse attack)

name.en: The idea of public-key cryptography: public and private keys
name.zh: 公钥密码的思路：公钥与私钥 (public-key cryptography, asymmetric keys)

name.en: Public-key management: certificates, CAs and PKI
name.zh: 公钥管理：证书与公钥基础设施 (certificates, CA, PKI)
数字签名的要求与做法 (digital signatures)
消息摘要与哈希 (message digest, hash function)

name.en: Authentication protocols: challenge-response and public-key authentication
name.zh: 认证协议：质询—应答与公钥认证 (authentication, challenge-response)

name.en: Diffie-Hellman key exchange and the man-in-the-middle attack
name.zh: Diffie-Hellman 密钥交换与中间人攻击 (Diffie-Hellman key exchange)

name.en: Symmetric-key and public-key algorithms and cipher modes
name.zh: 对称密钥、公钥算法与密码模式 (symmetric-key, public-key, cipher modes)
数字签名、身份认证与攻击 (digital signatures, authentication, attacks)

description.en: Thinking DES and AES come with ECB built in. They are block ciphers and can be paired with any mode; ECB is just the most naive one, and its flaw is that identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks.
description.zh: 以为 DES、AES 自带 ECB。它们是分组密码，可以配任何模式；ECB 只是最朴素的一种，缺点是相同明文块得到相同密文块。

description.en: Thinking the IV must be kept secret, or that it can be repeated freely. The IV need not be secret, but it must be random and never repeated; otherwise messages with the same beginning leak, and using the same (key, IV) twice invites a keystream reuse attack.
description.zh: 以为 IV 要保密，或者可以随便重复。IV 不必保密，但要随机、不重复，否则相同开头的消息会泄露，同一 (密钥, IV) 用两次更会招来密钥流重用攻击。

description.en: Thinking a signature is also “encrypt with the public key, decrypt with the private key”. A signature goes the other way: the private key processes, and the public key restores.
description.zh: 以为签名也是“公钥加密、私钥解密”。签名的方向相反：私钥处理，公钥还原。

description.en: Thinking it is enough to just send the digest. An attacker can replace a digest; only when the digest is signed is it tied to the sender.
description.zh: 以为直接发摘要就够了。摘要本身能被攻击者替换；要对摘要签名，它才和发信人绑在一起。

description.en: Treating Diffie-Hellman as an encryption algorithm. It only lets both sides compute the same secret on the spot; it does not prove who the other side is, so it can be attacked by a man in the middle.
description.zh: 把 Diffie-Hellman 当成加密算法。它只让双方现场算出同一个秘密，并不证明对方是谁，所以会被中间人攻击。

description.en: Thinking a public key fetched from the other party's website can be trusted. A public key can be swapped; you need a CA-signed certificate to bind a name to a public key.
description.zh: 以为从对方网站上拿到的公钥就可信。公钥可以被调包，要靠 CA 签名的证书把名字和公钥绑在一起。

chapter.en: Symmetric ciphers and modes of operation

title.en: Never met: how do you agree on a key?
title.zh: 没见过面，怎么约定钥匙

prompt.en: Alice and Bob have never met and share no secret. They can only talk over a public line, and Trudy listens the whole time. Can they agree on a key that only the two of them know?
prompt.zh: Alice 和 Bob 从没见过面，也没有任何共同的秘密。他们只能通过一条公开的线路说话，而 Trudy 全程在听。他们能不能约定出一把只有两人知道的钥匙？

label.en: Impossible: they must meet first to exchange a key
label.zh: 不可能：必须先见面交换钥匙

feedback.en: That is the intuition, but mathematics has a way around it. The second half of this lesson is about exactly that.
feedback.zh: 直觉上是这样，但数学上有办法绕过。这一课的后半就是它。

label.en: Possible: with an algorithm, each picks a secret number, they exchange a little public information, and each computes the same key
label.zh: 可能：靠一种算法，两人各出一个秘密数字，公开交换一点信息，各自算出同一把钥匙

feedback.en: Right, this is the Diffie-Hellman key exchange. The eavesdropper sees everything that passes between them but cannot compute the key.
feedback.zh: 对，这就是 Diffie-Hellman 密钥交换。偷听者看到了全部往来，却算不出钥匙。

label.en: Possible: Alice encrypts the key first and then sends it to Bob
label.zh: 可能：Alice 先把钥匙加密再发给 Bob

feedback.en: What key would she use to encrypt that key? That needs a previously shared key, so the problem just goes in circles.
feedback.zh: 用什么钥匙去加密这把钥匙？这又需要一把事先共享的钥匙，问题原地打转。

explain.en: The basic difficulty of symmetric cryptography is how to hand the key to the other party. This lesson first looks at symmetric ciphers themselves, then at how to get around that difficulty.
explain.zh: 对称密码的根本困难，就是钥匙怎么交给对方。这一课先看对称密码本身，再看怎样绕开这个困难。

title.en: Symmetric keys: the same key for both

text.en: Modern key-based algorithms fall into two families: **symmetric-key** and **public-key**. Symmetric means the same key encrypts and decrypts. Its methods share roots with the old ones from the previous lesson: permutation, substitution, or a combination of the two, just stacked over many rounds and far stronger.
text.zh: 现代密钥算法分两大类：**对称密钥** (symmetric-key) 和**公钥** (public-key)。对称的意思是加密和解密用同一把钥匙。它的手法和上一课的老办法同根：置换 (permutation)、替换 (substitution)，或两者组合，只是叠了很多轮，强度高得多。

text.en: DES and AES are both **block ciphers**: they cut the plaintext into blocks of a fixed size and encrypt it block by block.
text.zh: DES 和 AES 都是**分组密码** (block cipher)：把明文切成固定大小的块，一块一块加密。

title.en: Two things in the slides to watch
title.zh: 课件的写法有两处要留意

body.en: Triple DES uses three independent 56-bit keys, and its key space is usually given as $2^{168}$, not 3 × $2^{56}$. Standard AES has a fixed 128-bit block; only the key comes in three sizes: 128, 192 and 256 bits. In the exam, answer as the slides say, but know the real picture.
body.zh: 三重 DES 用三个独立的 56 位密钥，通常说密钥空间是 $2^{168}$，不是 3 × $2^{56}$。标准的 AES 分组固定为 128 位，只有密钥有 128、192、256 位三种。考试按课件的说法答，但要知道真实情况。

text.en: Symmetric ciphers are fast, but they have one fundamental difficulty: both sides must already hold the same key, so how is that key handed over safely? That problem is left to public-key cryptography. First, a closer problem: how is one key used to encrypt many blocks?
text.zh: 对称密码跑得快，但有一个根本困难：双方要先有同一把钥匙，这把钥匙怎么安全地交过去？这个问题留到公钥那里解决。先看一个更近的问题：一把钥匙怎样用来加密很多块。

title.en: The flaw of ECB, and CBC

text.en: The most naive approach is to encrypt every block on its own; this is called Electronic Code Book (ECB). It does not come with DES or AES; it is just one “mode of operation”. Its flaw: **identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks**.
text.zh: 最朴素的做法是每块各加密各的，叫电子密码本 (Electronic Code Book, ECB)。它不是 DES 或 AES 自带的，只是一种“工作模式”。它的毛病：**相同的明文块得到相同的密文块**。

text.en: For example, the approval results in a table are, in order: approve, approve, reject, approve. After ECB encryption the ciphertext blocks are X, X, Y, X. The attacker cannot read the content, but sees that blocks 1, 2 and 4 are the same, so the pattern of the plaintext leaks (an image encrypted with ECB still shows its outline clearly).
text.zh: 比如一份表格里的审批结果依次是：同意、同意、拒绝、同意。ECB 加密后密文块是 X、X、Y、X。攻击者读不懂内容，却看出第 1、2、4 块相同，明文的图案漏了出来（一张图片用 ECB 加密，轮廓依然清晰可见）。

text.en: **Cipher Block Chaining** (CBC) ties each block's result to the previous one: each plaintext block is first XORed with the **previous ciphertext block** and then encrypted. The first block has no previous block, so a randomly chosen **initialization vector** (IV) is used.
text.zh: **密码块链接** (Cipher Block Chaining, CBC) 让每块的结果牵连上一块：每个明文块先和**上一个密文块**异或，再加密。第一块没有上一块，就用一个随机选的**初始向量** (IV)。

blocks.tex: C_0 = E_K(P_0\oplus IV),\qquad C_i = E_K(P_i\oplus C_{i-1}),\qquad P_i = D_K(C_i)\oplus C_{i-1}

text.en: Even if $P_0 = P_1$, they are XORed with different things (one with the IV, one with $C_0$), so the ciphertexts differ and the pattern is gone. Why must the IV be random? Otherwise two messages with the same beginning would have the same first ciphertext block, leaking again that “the beginnings are the same”. The IV need not be secret, only random and never repeated.
text.zh: 即使 $P_0 = P_1$，它们异或的对象不同（一个是 IV，一个是 $C_0$），密文就不同，图案没了。IV 为什么要随机？否则两条开头相同的消息，第一块密文也相同，又泄露了“开头一样”。IV 不用保密，只要随机、不重复。

text.en: The price: encryption can only be done in order, since computing $C_i$ needs $C_{i-1}$ first.
text.zh: 代价：加密只能顺序做，算 $C_i$ 要先有 $C_{i-1}$。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: what happens if one ciphertext block is corrupted
summary.zh: 超出课件：一个密文块传错了会怎样

text.en: In CBC decryption, the corrupted block $C_i$ decrypts to a $P_i$ that is garbled throughout; the next block $P_{i+1}$ is wrong by just one bit at the corresponding position, and after that decryption returns to normal.
text.zh: CBC 解密时，坏的那块 $C_i$ 解出的 $P_i$ 整块是乱的，下一块 $P_{i+1}$ 只在对应的位置错一位，再往后恢复正常。

title.en: CFB: encrypting one byte at a time
title.zh: CFB：一个字节一个字节地加密

intro.en: When you type on a keyboard, characters come out one at a time, and you cannot wait to fill a whole block before sending. **Cipher Feedback** (CFB) works like this: a 64-bit (8-byte) shift register holds the last 8 ciphertext bytes. For each plaintext byte, the whole register is encrypted once, only the leftmost byte of the result is taken, and it is XORed with the plaintext byte to give the ciphertext byte. That ciphertext byte is sent out and also shifted into the register, pushing the oldest one out. The slides say: a 1-bit error in the ciphertext affects the decryption of 9 bytes. Let us work it out.
intro.zh: 敲键盘时，字一个一个出来，等不到凑满一个块再发。**密码反馈** (Cipher Feedback, CFB) 的做法：一个 64 位（8 字节）的移位寄存器放着最近 8 个密文字节。每来一个明文字节，就把寄存器整个加密一次，只取结果最左边的一个字节，与明文字节异或得到密文字节；这个密文字节送出去，同时移进寄存器，最旧的挤出。课件说：密文里 1 比特的错误会影响 9 字节的解密结果。我们来推一下。

why.en: At this moment the register holds the 8 ciphertext bytes $C_2$ to $C_9$, and Left takes the leftmost byte of the encryption result
why.zh: 此刻寄存器里是 $C_2$ 到 $C_9$ 共 8 个密文字节，Left 取加密结果最左一个字节

why.en: The receiver's register also holds the received ciphertext, so the same value is XORed back out
why.zh: 接收方的寄存器里装的也是收到的密文，所以用同一个值异或回去

lines.tex: C_{10}\text{ 错了 1 比特} \Rightarrow P_{10}\text{ 错 1 比特}

why.en: XOR carries the error unchanged to the same position in the plaintext; this is the 1st byte
why.zh: 异或把错误原样带到明文的同一位置，这是第 1 个字节

lines.tex: C_{10}\text{ 要待在寄存器里 8 次移位}

why.en: It enters the register from the right end and moves one place left with every new byte, so it is pushed out only after 8 shifts
why.zh: 它从寄存器右端进入，每来一个字节就左移一格，8 次后才被挤出

why.en: During those 8 shifts the register holds the bad byte, so the encryption result is completely different, and the next 8 bytes are all decrypted wrongly
why.zh: 这 8 次里，寄存器里都带着坏字节，加密结果全变，接下来 8 个字节全部解错

outro.en: The good side is that data can be encrypted even when it arrives one byte at a time; the price is that an error spreads over 9 bytes.
outro.zh: 好处是数据一个字节一个字节到也能加密；代价是错误会扩散到 9 个字节。

title.en: Stream cipher mode and counter mode
title.zh: 流密码模式与计数器模式

text.en: **Stream cipher mode**: the key and the IV are used to encrypt repeatedly, producing a long **keystream**. The keystream depends only on the key and the IV, **not on the data**, so it can be computed ahead of time. Use it as a one-time pad: XOR it with the plaintext to get the ciphertext, and XOR once more to decrypt.
text.zh: **流密码模式** (stream cipher mode)：由密钥和 IV 反复加密，产生一长串**密钥流** (keystream)。密钥流只取决于密钥和 IV，**与数据无关**，所以能提前算好。拿它当一次性密码本，与明文异或得到密文，解密时再异或一次。

text.en: **Counter mode** goes one step further: instead of encrypting the plaintext, it encrypts IV, IV+1, IV+2, and so on, and uses each result as the keystream for that block, XORed with the plaintext block. The keystream for block i depends only on i, not on any earlier block.
text.zh: **计数器模式** (counter mode) 更进一步：不去加密明文，而是加密 IV、IV+1、IV+2……每个结果当作那一块的密钥流，与明文块异或。第 i 块的密钥流只取决于 i，不依赖前面任何一块。

rows.en: Almost never use: identical blocks give identical ciphertext
rows.zh: 几乎不要用：相同块得到相同密文

rows.en: XOR with the previous ciphertext block, then encrypt
rows.zh: 先与上一密文块异或再加密

rows.en: Data processed block by block in order
Byte by byte, using a shift register of ciphertext
rows.zh: 逐字节，靠密文移位寄存器

rows.en: Data that does not arrive all at once, such as keyboard input
rows.zh: 键盘输入这类不是一次到齐的数据

rows.en: Keystream independent of the data, XOR
rows.zh: 密钥流与数据无关，异或

title.en: Dragging the progress bar

prompt.en: A 10 GB video file is stored encrypted, and while it plays the user drags the progress bar to any position at will. Which cipher mode is the best fit? Explain briefly.
prompt.zh: 一个 10 GB 的视频文件是加密存放的，播放时用户会随意拖进度条到任何位置。哪种密码模式最合适？简要说明理由。

key_points.en: The keystream for each block is computed from the IV plus its position number, with no dependence on earlier blocks, so you can jump straight to any position
key_points.zh: 每一块的密钥流由 IV 加上它的位置序号算出，不依赖前面的块，可直接定位到任意位置

key_points.en: Contrast: CFB needs several preceding ciphertext bytes, and stream cipher mode must produce the keystream from the start in order
key_points.zh: 对比：CFB 要前面若干密文字节，流密码模式要从头依次产生密钥流

model_answer.en: Counter mode is the best fit. It encrypts IV+i, so the keystream for block i depends only on its position and needs no earlier block, which means you can jump straight to any position to decrypt. CFB needs the preceding 8 bytes of ciphertext, and stream cipher mode must produce the keystream in order; neither is convenient for random access.
model_answer.zh: 计数器模式最合适。它加密的是 IV+i，第 i 块的密钥流只取决于它的位置，不需要前面的块，所以能直接跳到任意位置解密。CFB 需要前面 8 个字节的密文，流密码模式要依次产生密钥流，都不方便随机访问。

explain.en: For random access, each block must be able to compute its own keystream independently. Counter mode uses the position as the input.
explain.zh: 要随机访问，就要每一块都能独立算出自己的密钥流。计数器模式是用位置当输入。

title.en: Keystream reuse: using the same key twice
title.zh: 密钥流重用：同一把钥匙用两次

intro.en: Stream cipher mode and counter mode have a trap. If the same pair (key, IV) is used twice, the two keystreams $K_0$ are exactly the same. It is the same reason as the “use only once” rule for the one-time pad in the last lesson. Suppose an attacker intercepts two ciphertexts, which were encrypted from plaintexts $P_0$ and $Q_0$ with the same $K_0$. A numerical example:
intro.zh: 流密码模式和计数器模式有一个陷阱。如果同一对（密钥, IV）用了两次，两次产生的密钥流 $K_0$ 完全一样。这和上一课一次性密码本的“只能用一次”是同一个道理。设攻击者截到两条密文，它们分别由明文 $P_0$、$Q_0$ 用同一个 $K_0$ 加密。数字例：

why.en: Only the sender and receiver know $K_0$; the attacker does not
why.zh: $K_0$ 只有收发双方知道，攻击者不知道

why.en: The first ciphertext
why.zh: 第一条密文

why.en: The second ciphertext
why.zh: 第二条密文

lines.tex: C_1\oplus C_2 = (P_0\oplus K_0)\oplus(Q_0\oplus K_0) = P_0\oplus Q_0 = 00000001

why.en: The attacker just XORs the two ciphertexts: $K_0$ appears twice and cancels, leaving the XOR of the two plaintexts
why.zh: 攻击者只需把两条密文异或：$K_0$ 出现两次，抵消了，剩下两条明文的异或

why.en: If a short piece of one message is guessed or known (for example a fixed beginning), the other message at the same position comes out. Natural language has a lot that can be guessed
why.zh: 只要猜出或知道其中一条的一小段（比如固定的开头），另一条同一位置就出来了。自然语言里可猜的东西很多

outro.en: So the key and the IV must be chosen independently and at random, and never repeated. The keystream itself is single-use.
outro.zh: 所以密钥和 IV 要独立、随机地选，绝不重复。密钥流本身是一次性的。

title.en: Know one, deduce the other

prompt.en: Two messages are encrypted with the same (key, IV), and the ciphertexts of their first bytes are 11100011 and 11100000. The attacker knows that the first plaintext byte of the first message is T (01010100). What is the first plaintext byte of the second message?
prompt.zh: 两条消息用同一对（密钥, IV）加密，首字节的密文分别是 11100011 和 11100000。攻击者知道第一条的首字节明文是 T（01010100）。第二条的首字节明文是什么？

feedback.en: Right. XORing the two ciphertexts gives 00000011, which equals the XOR of the two plaintexts; XOR that with T to get 01010111, which is W.
feedback.zh: 对。两条密文异或得 00000011，等于两条明文的异或；再与 T 异或，得 01010111，是 W。

feedback.en: The two ciphertexts differ, so the plaintexts differ.
feedback.zh: 两条密文不同，说明明文不同。

label.en: Cannot be computed, because the keystream is unknown
label.zh: 算不出来，因为不知道密钥流

feedback.en: You do not need to know the keystream: XORing the two ciphertexts cancels it.
feedback.zh: 不需要知道密钥流：两条密文一异或，密钥流就抵消了。

title.en: Public key: separating the lock from the key

text.en: The fundamental difficulty of symmetric cryptography: both sides must first hold the same key, and handing over a key securely needs a secure channel in the first place. With more people it gets worse: n people communicating privately in pairs need n(n−1)/2 keys, which for 100 people is 4950.
text.zh: 对称密码的根本困难：双方要先有同一把钥匙，而要安全地交钥匙，又得先有一条安全的通道。人一多更糟：n 个人两两私下通信，需要 n(n−1)/2 把钥匙，100 人就是 4950 把。

text.en: Diffie and Hellman proposed **asymmetric keys**: two keys, where it is very hard to derive one from the other. Think of a mailbox: anyone can drop a letter into the slot (the **public key**, available to everyone, used to encrypt messages to its owner); only the owner holds the key that opens the box (the **private key**, known only to the owner, used to decrypt).
text.zh: Diffie 与 Hellman 提出了**非对称密钥** (asymmetric keys)：用两把钥匙，而且从一把很难推出另一把。像一个邮筒：任何人都能往投信口里扔信（**公钥**，人人可得，用来加密发给其主人的消息）；只有主人拿着开箱的钥匙（**私钥**，只有主人知道，用来解密）。

blocks.tex: C = E_{K_1}(P),\qquad P = D_{K_2}(C),\qquad D_{K_2}\bigl(E_{K_1}(P)\bigr) = P

text.en: $K_1$ is the public key and $K_2$ is the private key. The sender needs only the public key and the plaintext to encrypt; only the receiver holding the private key can undo the effect of $K_1$.
text.zh: $K_1$ 是公钥，$K_2$ 是私钥。发送方只需要知道公钥和明文，就能加密；只有持私钥的接收方能撤销 $K_1$ 的效果。

text.en: The intuition behind “hard to derive from each other”: some operations are easy forwards and extremely hard backwards. For example, multiplying two large primes is easy, but splitting the product back apart is extremely hard. The private key is like a secret passage: with it, going backwards becomes easy.
text.zh: “不易互推”的直觉：有些运算正着做很容易，倒着做极难。比如把两个大素数相乘很容易，把乘积拆回去极难。私钥就像一条暗道：知道它，倒着做就容易了。

title.en: Don't mix up the names

body.en: The slides call public-key encryption the “Diffie-Hellman key system”, meaning the idea Diffie and Hellman proposed. The “Diffie-Hellman key exchange” later on is a different, specific algorithm: it encrypts nothing, it only lets both sides compute the same secret.
body.zh: 课件把公钥加密叫“Diffie-Hellman key system”，指的是 Diffie 和 Hellman 提出的这个想法。后面的“Diffie-Hellman 密钥交换”是另一个具体的算法：它不加密任何东西，只让双方算出同一个秘密。

title.en: RSA: how to make a key pair

text.en: RSA (Rivest, Shamir, Adleman) is the most common public-key algorithm. The steps to make the keys:
text.zh: RSA（Rivest、Shamir、Adleman）是最常见的公钥算法。造钥匙的步骤：

items.en: Choose two large primes p and q.
Choose a d that is coprime to z (no common factor).
items.zh: 选一个与 z 互素的 d（没有公因子）。

items.en: Find e such that $(d\times e)\bmod z = 1$.
items.zh: 找 e 使 $(d\times e)\bmod z = 1$。

items.en: The **public key** is (e, n) and the **private key** is (d, n).

blocks.tex: C = P^{e}\bmod n,\qquad P = C^{d}\bmod n

text.en: The plaintext P must be smaller than n; larger messages must first be cut into small blocks. Security rests on “factoring a large number is hard”: n is public, but to get z you first have to split n into p×q.
text.zh: 明文 P 必须小于 n，大的要先切成小块。安全性靠“分解大数很难”：n 是公开的，但要算出 z，就得先把 n 拆成 p×q。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: why C^d restores P
summary.zh: 超出课件：为什么 C^d 能还原 P

text.en: From $(d\times e)\bmod z = 1$ we get $d\times e = 1 + kz$. Euler's theorem in number theory says $P^z\equiv 1 \pmod n$ (when P and n are coprime), so $P^{de} = P\cdot(P^z)^k \equiv P \pmod n$. Encrypting and then decrypting is raising to a power twice, the exponents combine to $d\times e$, and P comes back.
text.zh: 由 $(d\times e)\bmod z = 1$，得 $d\times e = 1 + kz$。数论里的欧拉定理说 $P^z\equiv 1 \pmod n$（P 与 n 互素时），所以 $P^{de} = P\cdot(P^z)^k \equiv P \pmod n$。加密再解密就是乘方两次，指数合起来是 $d\times e$，P 就回来了。

title.en: Working RSA through: p = 3, q = 11

intro.en: The small example from the slides, encrypting SUZANNE one letter at a time. Letters are numbered by alphabet position (S is the 19th).
intro.zh: 课件的小例子，把 SUZANNE 一个字母一个字母加密。字母按字母表编号（S 是第 19 个）。

why.en: n is public, z is secret
why.zh: n 公开，z 保密

why.en: 7 and 20 have no common factor
why.zh: 7 与 20 没有公因子

why.en: Finding e: try e = 1, 2, 3; the products are 7, 14, 21, and 21 divided by 20 leaves remainder 1
The public key is made public; the private key is kept to yourself
why.zh: 公钥公开，私钥自己留着

why.en: Encryption: $P^3\bmod 33$
why.zh: 加密：$P^3\bmod 33$

why.en: Decryption: $C^7\bmod 33$. 28 is 5 less than 33, so it can be treated as −5; −78125 divided by 33 leaves remainder 19, which gets us back to S
why.zh: 解密：$C^7\bmod 33$。28 比 33 小 5，可当作 −5 来算；−78125 除以 33 余 19，就回到了 S

outro.en: The other letters work the same way: U's 21 encrypts to 21 again, Z's 26 becomes 20, A's 1 stays 1, N's 14 becomes 5, and E's 5 becomes 26. Notice two flaws: U is unchanged by encryption, and the two N's get the same ciphertext 5. The numbers are too small, and the same plaintext always gives the same ciphertext, which has the same root as ECB's flaw. (Real RSA uses numbers hundreds of digits long and adds random padding first; that is beyond the slides.) RSA is too slow for large amounts of data, so it is often used to distribute symmetric keys safely: Alice randomly makes a symmetric key, encrypts it with Bob's public key and sends it over, and all the data after that goes through a symmetric algorithm. The slides also say that factoring a 500-digit number takes about $10^{25}$ years, with no source, so read it only as “extremely long”.
outro.zh: 其余字母同理：U 的 21 加密后还是 21，Z 的 26 变成 20，A 的 1 还是 1，N 的 14 变成 5，E 的 5 变成 26。注意两个毛病：U 加密后没变，两个 N 得到同样的密文 5。数字太小，而且同样的明文总得到同样的密文，这和 ECB 的缺点同源。（真正的 RSA 用几百位的数，并先加随机填充；这是超出课件的。）RSA 对大量数据太慢，所以常用来安全地分发对称钥匙：Alice 随机造一把对称密钥，用 Bob 的公钥加密发过去，之后的数据全用对称算法传。课件还说分解 500 位的数大约要 $10^{25}$ 年，没有出处，只当“极其漫长”理解。

title.en: Finding e

prompt.en: Take p = 5, q = 11. Choose d = 3. Find the smallest positive integer e satisfying (d × e) mod z = 1.
prompt.zh: 取 p = 5，q = 11。选 d = 3。求满足 (d × e) mod z = 1 的最小正整数 e。

hints.en: First compute n = 55 and z = (5−1)×(11−1). Then find e such that 3e divided by z leaves remainder 1.

explain.en: z = 4 × 10 = 40. 3 × 27 = 81 = 2 × 40 + 1, remainder 1, so e = 27. No e smaller than 27 works: the remainder of 3e divided by 40 never reaches 1.

title.en: Digital signatures: four things to prove
title.zh: 数字签名：要证明的四件事

text.en: Encryption only provides secrecy; it cannot prove who sent something. A **digital signature** guarantees three things: authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation. Broken into four requirements:
text.zh: 加密只管保密，它不能证明谁发的。**数字签名** (digital signature) 保证三样东西：真实性 (authenticity)、完整性 (integrity)、不可否认性 (non-repudiation)。拆成四条要求：

items.en: The receiver can verify the identity the sender claims. (Authenticity)
items.zh: 收方能验证发方声称的身份。（真实性）

items.en: Both sides can verify the message was not changed in transit. (Integrity)
items.zh: 双方能验证消息在传输中没被改过。（完整性）

items.en: The receiver cannot forge messages. (The slides label this integrity, but it is really about stopping the receiver from impersonating the sender.)
items.zh: 收方不能自己伪造消息。（课件标成完整性，其实是防止收方冒充发方）

items.en: The sender cannot deny having sent it. (Non-repudiation)
items.zh: 发方不能否认自己发过。（不可否认性）

text.en: Symmetric keys can also do signatures, but they need a central “Big Brother” (BB) whom everyone trusts:
text.zh: 对称密钥也能做签名，但要一个居中的“大哥”(Big Brother, BB)，所有人都信任他：

rows.en: Using the key she shares with BB, Alice tells BB: I want to send P to B. $R_A$ is a random number and t is a timestamp
rows.zh: Alice 用自己和 BB 的共享钥匙，告诉 BB：我要把 P 发给 B。$R_A$ 是随机数，t 是时间戳

rows.en: BB decrypts and forwards to Bob, attaching its own “seal”: Alice sent P at time t
rows.zh: BB 解开后转给 Bob，并附上自己的“盖章”：Alice 在 t 时发过 P

text.en: $R_A$ and t guard against replay: if Trudy sends an old message again, BB and Bob will notice that the random number was already used and the time is too old. The price is that BB sees every message and must be trusted unconditionally.
text.zh: $R_A$ 和 t 是防重放用的：Trudy 把旧消息再发一遍，BB 和 Bob 会发现随机数用过了、时间也太旧。代价是 BB 看得见所有消息，必须无条件被信任。

title.en: Public-key signatures: sign with the private key, verify with the public key
title.zh: 公钥签名：私钥签，公钥验

intro.en: The public-key way needs no Big Brother: Alice processes P with her **private key**, and Bob restores it with Alice's **public key**. Note the direction is opposite to encryption: encryption locks with the public key and opens with the private key; signing signs with the private key and verifies with the public key. Only Alice has the private key, so only she can produce this result, and she cannot deny it. Borrowing the small RSA example, let Alice's public key be (3, 33), her private key (7, 33), and the P to sign be 19.
intro.zh: 公钥的做法不需要大哥：Alice 用自己的**私钥**处理 P，Bob 用 Alice 的**公钥**还原。注意方向和加密相反：加密是公钥锁、私钥开；签名是私钥签、公钥验。只有 Alice 有私钥，所以只有她造得出这个结果，她也抵赖不了。借用 RSA 小例，设 Alice 的公钥 (3, 33)，私钥 (7, 33)，要签的 P = 19。

why.en: Alice processes P with her private key. $19^2 = 361\equiv -2$, $19^6\equiv -8$, $19^7\equiv -152\equiv 13$
why.zh: Alice 用私钥处理 P。$19^2 = 361\equiv -2$，$19^6\equiv -8$，$19^7\equiv -152\equiv 13$

why.en: Bob restores with Alice's public key (3, 33) and gets P back, which shows S must have come from the owner of the private key
why.zh: Bob 用 Alice 的公钥 (3, 33) 还原，得回 P，说明 S 一定来自私钥的主人

why.en: In the slides' figure, Bob's public key is wrapped around the outside as well, giving secrecy at the same time. Bob first removes the outer layer with his own private key $D_B$, then verifies the signature with $E_A$. D_A is about “who”, E_B is about “who can read”
why.zh: 课件图里再外套 Bob 的公钥：同时保密。Bob 先用自己的私钥 $D_B$ 拆外层，再用 $E_A$ 验签。D_A 管“是谁”，E_B 管“谁能看”

outro.en: This uses a property of RSA: both orders restore the original. The signature itself is not secret, and anyone with the public key can verify it; for secrecy you must encrypt separately.
outro.zh: 这里用到了 RSA 的一个性质：两种顺序都能还原。签名本身不保密，任何有公钥的人都能验；要保密得另外加密。

title.en: Message digest: a fingerprint for a long message
title.zh: 消息摘要：给长消息一个指纹

text.en: Processing a whole message with the private key is too slow and too long. A **message digest** (MD) uses a **one-way hash function** to turn plaintext of any length into a short bit string of fixed length, like a fingerprint of the message. It has four properties:
text.zh: 整条消息都拿私钥处理太慢、太长。**消息摘要** (message digest, MD) 用一个**单向哈希函数** (one-way hash function)，把任意长的明文变成固定长度的短比特串，像消息的指纹。它有四条性质：

items.en: Given P, computing MD(P) is easy.
items.zh: 由 P 算 MD(P) 很容易。

items.en: Given MD(P), it is practically impossible to work back to P.
items.zh: 由 MD(P) 几乎不可能反推 P。

items.en: Given P, nobody can find another P' with MD(P') = MD(P).
items.zh: 给定 P，没人能找到另一个 P' 使 MD(P') = MD(P)。

items.en: Changing even 1 bit of the input changes the output greatly.
items.zh: 输入哪怕只改 1 比特，输出也大不相同。

text.en: To sign, Alice sends P and $D_A(MD(P))$: the message goes in the clear as usual, and only the short digest is signed. Bob computes the digest of P, then restores the digest inside the signature with Alice's public key, and passes the check if the two agree. Property 3 is exactly why it can stand in for the whole message: if Trudy tries to swap the message, the digest will not match; property 4 says that a tiny change makes the digest unrecognizable.
text.zh: 签名时，Alice 发出 P 和 $D_A(MD(P))$：消息照旧明文发，只对短短的摘要签名。Bob 算出 P 的摘要，再用 Alice 的公钥还原签名里的摘要，两者一致就通过。第 3 条正是它能代替整条消息的原因：Trudy 想换一条消息，摘要就对不上；第 4 条说明改动一点点，摘要就面目全非。

text.en: Why **sign** the digest instead of just sending it? Because anyone can compute a digest. Trudy replaces P with P' and attaches the digest of P', and Bob still verifies it as fine. Only when it is signed with Alice's private key is the digest tied to her.
text.zh: 为什么要对摘要**签名**，而不是直接发摘要？因为摘要谁都能算。Trudy 把 P 换成 P'，再附上 P' 的摘要，Bob 照样验证通过。只有用 Alice 的私钥签过，摘要才和她绑在一起。

text.en: Common hash algorithms are SHA-1, SHA-2 and SHA-3. MD5 is known to have serious flaws, such as hash collisions (two different messages that give the same digest). The slides' example: the MD5 of “this is a test” is 54b0c58c7ce9f2a8b551351102ee0938, and its SHA-1 is fa26be19de6bff93f70bc2308434e4a440bbad02. However long the input, the output length is fixed.
text.zh: 常用的哈希算法有 SHA-1、SHA-2、SHA-3。MD5 已知有严重漏洞，比如哈希碰撞（两条不同的消息得到同一个摘要）。课件的例子：“this is a test”的 MD5 是 54b0c58c7ce9f2a8b551351102ee0938，SHA-1 是 fa26be19de6bff93f70bc2308434e4a440bbad02。输入再长，输出的长度也是固定的。

title.en: Beyond the slides

body.en: SHA-1 is also no longer considered secure (collisions have actually been constructed). The slides list it alongside SHA-2 and SHA-3, but in practice you should use the latter two.
body.zh: SHA-1 现在也已不再被认为安全（已有人实际构造出了碰撞），课件把它和 SHA-2、SHA-3 并列，实际应当用后两者。

title.en: Why not just send the digest

prompt.en: Alice wants Bob to be sure the message came from her. Can she simply send P and MD(P) together? Why must MD(P) be signed?
prompt.zh: Alice 想让 Bob 确信消息是她发的。她可以直接把 P 和 MD(P) 一起发过去吗？为什么要对 MD(P) 签名？

label.en: No: anyone can compute a digest, so Trudy can send P' with MD(P') instead; the signature is what ties the digest to Alice
label.zh: 不行：摘要谁都能算，Trudy 可以换成 P' 和 MD(P') 一起发，签名才把摘要和 Alice 绑在一起

feedback.en: Right. Without a signature, a digest only guards against accidental damage, not against deliberate replacement.
feedback.zh: 对。没有签名，摘要只能防“意外损坏”，防不了有人故意替换。

label.en: No: the digest is longer than the message, which is hard to send
label.zh: 不行：摘要比消息长，不好传

feedback.en: The digest is a fixed-length short bit string, much shorter than the message.
feedback.zh: 摘要是固定的短比特串，比消息短得多。

label.en: No: Bob has to restore the original message from the digest, so it must be encrypted
label.zh: 不行：Bob 要从摘要还原出原消息，必须加密

feedback.en: A one-way hash cannot give back the message at all; that is exactly its property 2.
feedback.zh: 单向哈希根本还原不回消息，这正是它的第 2 条性质。

explain.en: The digest provides the “fingerprint”, and the signature provides “this is Alice's fingerprint”. You need both.
explain.zh: 摘要提供“指纹”，签名提供“这是 Alice 的指纹”。缺哪个都不行。

title.en: Can the public key you got be trusted?

text.en: All the public-key methods so far rest on one assumption: the public key in your hand really is the other party's. But where do you get it? Is it fine to put it on the other party's personal website?
text.zh: 前面所有公钥做法都有一个前提：你手里的公钥确实是对方的。可你从哪里拿到它？放在对方的个人网站上，行吗？

rows.en: Alice goes to fetch Bob's home page
rows.zh: Alice 去取 Bob 的主页

rows.en: Trudy intercepts and returns a fake home page carrying Trudy's own public key $E_T$
rows.zh: Trudy 拦住，返回一个假主页，上面放着 Trudy 自己的公钥 $E_T$

rows.en: Alice encrypts her message with $E_T$ and sends it; Trudy intercepts it, opens it with her own private key and reads it
rows.zh: Alice 用 $E_T$ 加密消息发出，Trudy 拦下，用自己的私钥解开读完

rows.en: Trudy then encrypts it with Bob's real public key $E_B$ and forwards it to Bob
rows.zh: Trudy 再用 Bob 真正的公钥 $E_B$ 加密，转给 Bob

text.en: Neither Alice nor Bob notices anything, and Trudy sees it all. This is the **man-in-the-middle attack**, in the same position as the Equifax case in the last lesson. The problem is not the cryptographic algorithm, but that the public key itself carries no proof of identity.
text.zh: Alice 和 Bob 都毫无察觉，Trudy 全部看光。这就是**中间人攻击**，和上一课 Equifax 的位置一样。问题不在密码算法，而在公钥本身没有身份证明。

text.en: What about building a “key distribution center” that hands out public keys on demand? The slides leave this question open. Such a center must be trusted by everyone, must be online every time, becomes a bottleneck, and if it is compromised the whole system falls. The next page has a better way: let the center stamp things offline instead of delivering them online.
text.zh: 那建一个“密钥分发中心”，按需发公钥呢？课件留了这个问题。这样一个中心要被所有人信任、每次都要在线，一旦被攻破整个系统都完蛋，也是瓶颈。下一页是更好的办法：让中心离线盖章，而不是在线递送。

title.en: Certificates and PKI

text.en: The answer is the **certificate**: a trusted **Certification Authority** (CA) first verifies your identity by non-electronic means (such as checking an ID or meeting in person), then **binds your name to your public key** and signs it with the CA's private key. The format is specified by X.509. The slides' example takes a SHA-1 digest of the whole certificate and signs it with the CA's private key (nowadays a stronger hash is used, but the principle is the same).
text.zh: 办法是**证书** (certificate)：由可信的**认证机构** (Certification Authority, CA) 先用非电子的方式（比如看证件、见面）核实你的身份，再把你的**名字和公钥绑在一起**，用 CA 的私钥签名。格式由 X.509 规定。课件里的例子是对整份证书做 SHA-1 摘要，再用 CA 私钥签名（现在用更强的哈希，原理一样）。

text.en: To verify, check the signature with the CA's public key. If Trudy tries to slip a fake public key into a certificate, she must change either the name or the public key, and the digest changes at once; she does not have the CA's private key and so cannot sign again, so verification fails.
text.zh: 验证时，用 CA 的公钥验签。Trudy 想把假公钥塞进证书，要么改名字、要么改公钥，摘要立刻变；她又没有 CA 的私钥，没法重新签，验签就会失败。

text.en: Where does the CA's public key come from? CAs form a hierarchy, which makes up the **Public Key Infrastructure** (PKI): the Root signs for the RAs below it, the RAs sign for the CAs, and the CAs sign for users. The parts are users, CAs, certificates, and a directory that stores the certificates.
text.zh: CA 的公钥又从哪来？CA 组成层级，构成**公钥基础设施** (Public Key Infrastructure, PKI)：根 (Root) 为下一级的 RA 签名，RA 再为 CA 签名，CA 再为用户签名。组成部分有用户、CA、证书和存放证书的目录 (directory)。

alt.en: The Root signs for RA 2, RA 2 signs for CA 5, and CA 5 signs for Bob's certificate, forming a chain of trust
alt.zh: 根为 RA 2 签名，RA 2 为 CA 5 签名，CA 5 为 Bob 的证书签名，形成一条信任链

text.en: To verify Bob's certificate, follow the chain upwards: each link is verified with the public key of the one above it, until you reach a root that you trusted in advance.
text.zh: 验证 Bob 的证书，顺着链往上，每一环都用上一环的公钥验签，直到遇到一个你事先就信任的根。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: why the root's public key can be trusted, and what if a certificate is revoked
summary.zh: 超出课件：根的公钥凭什么可信，证书被撤销怎么办

text.en: Nobody signs for the root, so the root's public key is installed in advance in the operating system or browser, and trust starts from there. Certificates also have validity periods and can be revoked if something goes wrong. The slides do not go into either.
text.zh: 没有人给根签名，所以根的公钥是事先装在操作系统或浏览器里的，信任从这里开始。证书也有有效期，出了问题可以被撤销。课件都没有展开。

title.en: Authentication: challenge-response

text.en: **Authentication** means confirming that the other party in a communication is who they claim to be. It usually takes several messages back and forth, and along the way sets up the **session key** for this communication.
text.zh: **认证** (authentication) 是确认通信对方就是它声称的那个人。通常要来回交换几条消息，顺带建立这次通信用的**会话密钥** (session key)。

text.en: A basic principle: use long-term keys as little as possible, and pick a fresh random session key for each connection. The reason: the more a long-term key is used, the more ciphertext is intercepted and the greater the chance of exposure; if a session key leaks, only that one session is affected.
text.zh: 一个基本原则：尽量少用长期密钥，每次连接随机选一把新的会话密钥。理由：长期密钥用得越多，被截获的密文越多，暴露的机会越大；会话密钥即使泄露，也只影响这一次。

text.en: When Alice and Bob already have a shared key $K_{AB}$, they use **challenge-response**. $R_A$ and $R_B$ are challenges each side picks at random:
text.zh: Alice 和 Bob 已有共享密钥 $K_{AB}$ 时，用**质询—应答** (challenge-response)。$R_A$、$R_B$ 是双方各自随机选的质询：

rows.en: I am Alice (just a claim, no proof)
rows.zh: 我是 Alice（只是声明，没有证明）

rows.en: Alice answers with the shared key, and Bob confirms she is Alice
rows.zh: Alice 用共享钥匙答题，Bob 由此确认她是 Alice

rows.en: Alice also sets a random question
Bob answers, and Alice confirms he is Bob
rows.zh: Bob 答题，Alice 由此确认他是 Bob

text.en: The key is never sent directly; it only proves “I have it”. Why must the challenge be **random**? If the question were fixed, Trudy could record one answer and replay it every time afterwards. With a fresh random question, an old answer is worthless. Why must the two sides **verify each other**? If only one side is verified, the other may still be talking to an impersonator.
text.zh: 钥匙从来没有直接发出去，只证明了“我有它”。为什么质询要**随机**？如果题目是固定的，Trudy 录下一次答案，以后每次重放就行。随机的新题，旧答案就无效。为什么要**双方互相验证**？只验一方，另一方仍可能在和冒充者说话。

title.en: Public-key authentication: what each of the seven messages proves
title.zh: 公钥认证：七条消息各证明什么

text.en: When the two sides share no key but each has a public key, public-key authentication is used, and it also negotiates the session key $K_S$ along the way. $E_A$ and $E_B$ are the public keys of Alice and Bob, and the public-key certificates are fetched from the directory server (directory).
text.zh: 双方没有共享密钥，但各有公钥时，用公钥来认证，并顺带协商会话密钥 $K_S$。$E_A$、$E_B$ 是 Alice 和 Bob 的公钥，公钥证书从目录服务器 (directory) 取得。

rows.zh: Alice 拿到 Bob 的公钥（证书）

rows.en: Only Bob's private key can read it: I am Alice, and this is my random number
rows.zh: 只有 Bob 的私钥能读：我是 Alice，这是我的随机数
Bob 拿到 Alice 的公钥

rows.en: Only Alice's private key can read it: it returns $R_A$, then gives Bob's random number and the session key
rows.zh: 只有 Alice 的私钥能读：回传 $R_A$，再给出 Bob 的随机数和会话密钥

rows.en: Alice answers back $R_B$ with the session key

text.en: When can Alice be sure the other side is Bob? At message 6. Message 6 carries $R_A$, and $R_A$ appeared only in message 3, which was encrypted with $E_B$ and can be opened only by Bob's private key. Only Bob can send $R_A$ back unchanged.
text.zh: Alice 什么时候能确信对方是 Bob？第 6 条。第 6 条里带着 $R_A$，而 $R_A$ 只在第 3 条里出现过，那是用 $E_B$ 加密的，只有 Bob 的私钥才能解开。能把 $R_A$ 原样送回来的，只可能是 Bob。

text.en: Conversely, Bob has the same assurance only at message 7: $K_S(R_B)$ contains $R_B$, and $R_B$ appeared only in message 6, which was encrypted with $E_A$ and can be opened only by Alice. From then on, both sides communicate with $K_S$.
text.zh: 反过来，Bob 要到第 7 条才有同样的把握：$K_S(R_B)$ 里有 $R_B$，而 $R_B$ 只在第 6 条里出现过，那是用 $E_A$ 加密的，只有 Alice 能解开。此后双方用 $K_S$ 通信。

title.en: When is Bob sure

prompt.en: Still the public-key authentication protocol with the seven messages above. After which message can Bob be sure he is communicating with Alice? Explain briefly.
prompt.zh: 还是上面的七条消息的公钥认证协议。Bob 在哪条消息之后，才能确信自己是在和 Alice 通信？简要说明理由。

key_points.en: $K_S(R_B)$ in message 7 contains $R_B$, and $R_B$ appears only in message 6
key_points.zh: 第 7 条里的 $K_S(R_B)$ 含有 $R_B$，而 $R_B$ 只出现在第 6 条里

key_points.en: Message 6 was encrypted with Alice's public key $E_A$, so only Alice, who holds the private key, can open it and take out $R_B$ and $K_S$
key_points.zh: 第 6 条是用 Alice 的公钥 $E_A$ 加密的，只有持有私钥的 Alice 能解开，从中取出 $R_B$ 和 $K_S$

model_answer.en: After message 7. Message 7, $K_S(R_B)$, contains the random number $R_B$ that Bob put in message 6 and the session key $K_S$; message 6 was encrypted with Alice's public key, and only Alice's private key can open it, so only Alice can send $R_B$ back.
model_answer.zh: 第 7 条之后。第 7 条消息 $K_S(R_B)$ 里有 Bob 在第 6 条里放的随机数 $R_B$ 和会话密钥 $K_S$；第 6 条是用 Alice 的公钥加密的，只有 Alice 的私钥能解开，所以能送回 $R_B$ 的只可能是 Alice。

explain.en: Alice is sure the other side is Bob after message 6, because only Bob's private key can read the $R_A$ in message 3. Bob's case is the mirror image: he must wait for message 7, which shows the other side read message 6, readable only by Alice.
explain.zh: Alice 在第 6 条之后确信对方是 Bob，原因是只有 Bob 的私钥能读第 3 条里的 $R_A$。Bob 的情形是镜像：要等第 7 条，才证明对方读到了只有 Alice 能读的第 6 条。

title.en: Diffie-Hellman: working it through with small numbers

intro.en: Back to the start: with no shared key, how do you make one on the spot over a public line? Alice and Bob first publicly agree on two large numbers n and g. Alice secretly picks x and sends $g^x\bmod n$; Bob secretly picks y and sends $g^y\bmod n$. What each then computes is the same number $g^{xy}\bmod n$. Let us pick small numbers ourselves: n = 23, g = 5, x = 6, y = 15.
intro.zh: 回到开头：没有共享密钥，怎么在公开的线上现场造一把？Alice 和 Bob 先公开约定两个大数 n 和 g。Alice 秘密选 x，发出 $g^x\bmod n$；Bob 秘密选 y，发出 $g^y\bmod n$。各自算出的，是同一个数 $g^{xy}\bmod n$。我们自己选小数字：n = 23，g = 5，x = 6，y = 15。

why.en: What Alice sends. $5^2 = 25\equiv 2$, so $5^6 = 2^3 = 8$
What Bob sends. $5^{12}\equiv 8^2 = 64\equiv 18$, $5^3 = 125\equiv 10$, $18\times 10 = 180\equiv 19$
Alice computes with her own x: $19\equiv -4$, $(-4)^2 = 16$, $(-4)^4 = 256\equiv 3$, $(-4)^6\equiv 3\times 16 = 48\equiv 2$
why.zh: Alice 用自己的 x 算：$19\equiv -4$，$(-4)^2 = 16$，$(-4)^4 = 256\equiv 3$，$(-4)^6\equiv 3\times 16 = 48\equiv 2$

why.en: Bob computes with his own y: $8^2 \equiv -5$, $8^4\equiv 2$, $8^8\equiv 4$, $8^{12}\equiv 8$, $8^3 = 512\equiv 6$, $8^{15}\equiv 8\times 6 = 48\equiv 2$
why.zh: Bob 用自己的 y 算：$8^2 \equiv -5$，$8^4\equiv 2$，$8^8\equiv 4$，$8^{12}\equiv 8$，$8^3 = 512\equiv 6$，$8^{15}\equiv 8\times 6 = 48\equiv 2$

why.en: Both sides get the same shared secret, 2, because the order of exponentiation can be swapped
why.zh: 两边得到同一个共享秘密 2，因为乘方的次序可以交换

outro.en: The eavesdropper sees n = 23, g = 5 and the two numbers that passed between them, 8 and 19, but to get 2 they would need to know x or y, that is, work x back from $5^x\equiv 8 \pmod{23}$. This is called the discrete logarithm problem. With tiny numbers, trying them one by one takes a few hours at most; the real numbers have hundreds of digits, and there is no known fast method. Like RSA, it relies on “easy forwards, extremely hard backwards”.
outro.zh: 偷听者看到了 n = 23、g = 5 和两个往来的数 8、19，但要算出 2，就得知道 x 或 y，也就是从 $5^x\equiv 8 \pmod{23}$ 反推 x。这叫离散对数问题。数小时一个个试就行，真实用的数有几百位，没有已知的快办法。它和 RSA 一样，靠的是“正着算容易，倒着算极难”。

title.en: Compute the shared secret yourself

prompt.en: n = 23, g = 5. Alice secretly picks x = 4 and Bob secretly picks y = 3. What is the shared secret $g^{xy}\bmod 23$ they end up with?
prompt.zh: n = 23，g = 5。Alice 秘密选 x = 4，Bob 秘密选 y = 3。他们最终得到的共享秘密 $g^{xy}\bmod 23$ 是多少？

hints.en: Alice sends $5^4\bmod 23$ and Bob sends $5^3\bmod 23$. Then each raises to the power of their own secret.
hints.zh: Alice 发出 $5^4\bmod 23$，Bob 发出 $5^3\bmod 23$。再用各自的秘密乘方。

explain.en: Alice sends $5^4 = 625\equiv 4$ and Bob sends $5^3 = 125\equiv 10$. Alice computes $10^4 \bmod 23 = 18$, and Bob computes $4^3 = 64\equiv 18$. Both sides get 18.
explain.zh: Alice 发出 $5^4 = 625\equiv 4$，Bob 发出 $5^3 = 125\equiv 10$。Alice 算 $10^4 \bmod 23 = 18$，Bob 算 $4^3 = 64\equiv 18$。两边都是 18。

title.en: Diffie-Hellman can be fooled by a man in the middle too

text.en: The slides ask: is there a way to break it? Yes, with Trudy standing in the middle:
text.zh: 课件问：有办法破解吗？有，Trudy 站在中间：

items.en: Alice sends $g^x\bmod n$ and Trudy intercepts it.
items.zh: Alice 发出 $g^x\bmod n$，被 Trudy 拦下。

items.en: Trudy picks a z of her own, poses as Alice and sends $g^z\bmod n$ to Bob.
items.zh: Trudy 自己选一个 z，冒充 Alice，向 Bob 发 $g^z\bmod n$。

items.en: Bob replies with $g^y\bmod n$, Trudy intercepts it, poses as Bob and replies to Alice with $g^z\bmod n$.
items.zh: Bob 回 $g^y\bmod n$，Trudy 拦下，又冒充 Bob，向 Alice 回 $g^z\bmod n$。

text.en: The result is that Alice and Trudy share one key, and Trudy and Bob share another. For every message in the session, Trudy first opens and reads it, then re-encrypts it with the other key and forwards it. The two notice nothing. The reason: DH only lets you compute the same secret with **someone**; it does not say who that someone is.
text.zh: 结果 Alice 和 Trudy 共享一把密钥，Trudy 和 Bob 共享另一把。会话里的每条消息 Trudy 都先解开读、再用另一把重新加密转发。两人毫无察觉。原因：DH 只让你和**某个人**算出同一个秘密，并没有说那个人是谁。

text.en: The fix: authenticate the values each side sends. Alice **signs** $g^x\bmod n$ with her own private key (and attaches her certificate), and Bob accepts it only if it verifies; Trudy has no private key of Alice's and cannot forge it. This ties together everything covered so far: certificates and signatures prove who you are, DH or RSA makes the session key on the spot, and a symmetric algorithm carries the bulk of the data. This is the idea behind HTTPS in the next lesson.
text.zh: 修补：认证双方发出的值。Alice 把 $g^x\bmod n$ 用自己的私钥**签名**（并附上证书），Bob 验得过才接受；Trudy 没有 Alice 的私钥，伪造不了。这样就把前面讲的东西串起来了：证书和签名证明你是谁，DH 或 RSA 现场造出会话密钥，再用对称算法传大量数据。这正是下一课 HTTPS 背后的思路。

rows.en: Swap the public key or the DH value, standing between the two sides
rows.zh: 换掉公钥或 DH 的值，站在两方之间

rows.en: The same (key, IV) used twice; XORing the ciphertexts cancels the keystream
rows.zh: 同一对（密钥, IV）用两次，密文一异或，密钥流抵消

rows.en: Keys and IVs random, independent, never repeated
rows.zh: 密钥和 IV 随机、独立、不重复

rows.en: Send an old message again unchanged
rows.zh: 把旧消息原样再发一遍

rows.en: A fresh random number or timestamp each time
rows.zh: 每次用新的随机数或时间戳
